pre_score_revision: v1 retained in runs/pre_score_v1. Independent mathematical review required explicit labeling of nu=1 as a limiting zero-baseline-tension case; no evaluation score had been calculated. Finite-input guards were strengthened. Grid and predictions are unchanged.
scope: Auxiliary scalar reproduction, NOT completion of the coupled geometric prediction gate
known_outcomes: The publication and exported evaluation outcomes were already inspected. This is computational withholding, not blind validation.
endpoint: maximum_shortening_um in BOTH calibration and evaluation

mechanical_null.geometry: Independent identical volume-conserving columns; no tissue embedding or bending output
mechanical_null.nu_endpoint: nu=1 is a declared zero-baseline surface/lateral tension limit, not an interior positive-baseline M0 parameter; included as limiting material sensitivity
mechanical_null.selection: minimum calibration sum of squared shortening residuals over the declared finite grid; no continuum optimality claim

comparators: calibration-only ordinary least squares with intercept
uncertainty: Height/material grid is a sensitivity analysis, NOT an identified set or confidence/prediction interval. No unknown specimen independence is assumed.
decision: Report all declared model scores without choosing a post-score winner. Scalar success cannot pass geometric prediction or establish novelty.
normalization: Published optical recruitment normalization supplied by source, calculated across experiments; no claim of train-only optical preprocessing.
limitations: Maximum shortening is not center displacement, curvature or a paired time-resolved apical/basal profile.
Independent heterogeneous cells can produce size-dependent maxima through order statistics.
No absolute force calibration, complete initial geometry, cell topology, specimen IDs or measurement uncertainty model are supplied by these source tables.
Endpoint equilibrium and affine recruitment-to-tension are explicit null hypotheses, not validated cellular kinetics.
